sentences.text: Initially offence under Sections 419 and 420 of IPC and Sections 3/4 o f the Recognized Examination Act was registered against 81 candidates who had taken admission in G.R. Medical College, Gwalior, in the year 2006, 2008, 2010 and 2012 vide Crime No.449/2013 at Police Station Jhansi Road, Gwalior, as their signatures were found mismatched from test admission card and the present applicant was not made accused.
Thereafter, under the directions of Hon'ble Supreme Court, the matter was handed over to the C.B.I.
Total 271 accused were found involved in the offence by the C.B.I.

The present appellant has been arrayed as accused as one of the conspirator/helper for securing selection of Pratap Singh Chaudhari & Rajendra Baskel in the PMT Examination conducted by VYAPAM in the year 2010.

After completion of investigation, Charge-sheet was filed on 31/01/2020 under Sections 120-B, 109, 201, 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 of IPC read with Sections 3D(1-2)/4 of the Recognized Examination Act in the concerned Court with due notice to the applicant, however, he did not appear before the concerned Court on the said date, therefore, arrest warrant has been issued against him.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He further submits that present applicant has never been arrested by CBI in the entire investigation.
He was called by the Investigation Officer.
He appeared and gave his statement.
He cooperated in the investigation.
Therefore, his arrest is not required in this case.

Now,
after completion of investigation, charge-sheet has been filed on 31/01/2020; however, present applicant could not appear before the concerned Court at the time of filing of charge-sheet.
Therefore, arrest warrant has been issued against him.

In the apprehension of his arrest, he filed an application under Section 438 Cr.P.C. before the trial Court for anticipatory bail which has been rejected by the trial Court vide order dated 15/04/2024.
It is further submitted that confinement may bring social disrepute and personal inconvenience.
He undertakes to cooperate during trial and abide by all the conditions as may be imposed by this Court.
On such premises, learned counsel prayed for grant of anticipatory bail.

5. Learned counsel appearing for CBI when specifically asked whether custody of this applicant is required or not for further investigation in this case, he submits that since investigation has been completed and charge-sheet has been filed, therefore, no further custody is required.

However,
learned counsel appearing for the CBI has placed reliance on the decision of Apex Court in the case of Lavesh vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2012) 8 SCC 730 by submitting that application filed by one of the accused namely Rajesh Kumar Sharma has been dismissed by this Court vide order dated 21/03/2024 passed in M.Cr.C. No.10743/2024.
6.

entities.text: Lavesh vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2012) 8 SCC 730
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case of Lavesh (Supra), he was denied the anticipatory bail because he was declared absconder by the trial Court as he was not available for interrogation as well as investigation but this is not the case of prosecution and the case of present applicant.
He did not appear before the trial Court on the date of filing of charge-sheet and therefore, arrest warrant has been issued against him.
He has not been declared as absconder under the provision of Section 82 of Cr.P.C.

Therefore,
objection of learned counsel for respondent- CBI is rejected.
7 . Let the present applicant appear before the trial Court along with regular bail application.
The same shall be decided on the same day.
